executive_summary: The 30th parliamentary session on January 14, 2026 focused primarily on Dutch arms export policy, with 85 topics debated and 59 decisions reached. Key debates centered on weapons embargoes against Israel and Sudan, export controls, and humanitarian aid policy, with the government maintaining a case-by-case assessment approach against opposition calls for blanket restrictions. Multiple motions on strict export limitations were advised against, while measures on Sudan weapons diversion were referred to parliament for further consideration.

main_topics.summary: Parliament debated measures to prevent weapons diversion from Netherlands to Sudan through stricter export controls and enhanced end-user verification systems. DENK and SP argued that current export verification mechanisms are inadequate and weapons diversion cannot be completely excluded. The government acknowledged system limitations but argued it already conducts case-by-case risk assessments.

party_positions.DENK (Van Baarle): Support stricter controls despite acknowledging flaws in current export verification systems
party_positions.SP (Dobbe): Support measures to stop weapons flows to Sudan and review Netherlands' own export policy
party_positions.Government (De Vries): Already reviews licenses case-by-case and considers diversion risks; additional restrictions may be unnecessary

main_topics.outcome: Motion 22054 nr. 470 and 22054 nr. 474 referred to parliament (Oordeel Kamer) for further consideration

main_topics.summary: Contentious debate over whether to establish a complete and permanent weapons embargo against Israel versus maintaining a case-by-case assessment approach. DENK argued the International Court of Justice findings on genocide risk obligate the Netherlands to implement a blanket embargo under the Genocide Convention. The government opposed a blanket embargo, arguing defensive items like Iron Dome components should continue to be supplied based on individual assessments.

party_positions.DENK (Van Baarle): Advocate for complete and permanent weapons embargo based on ICJ genocide risk findings and Genocide Convention obligations
party_positions.Government (De Vries): Oppose blanket embargo; assess each case individually while supplying defensive items like Iron Dome components

main_topics.outcome: Motion 22054 nr. 471 on complete weapons embargo advised against (Ontraden)

main_topics.summary: GroenLinks-PvdA pressed for re-evaluation of Indonesian weapons export licenses based on investigative journalism evidence of military human rights abuses. The government emphasized it reviews multiple sources in case-by-case assessments but refused to commit to specific re-evaluation based on the Pointer investigation.

party_positions.GroenLinks-PvdA (Kröger): Request concrete re-evaluation of Indonesia export licenses based on documented human rights abuses
party_positions.Government (De Vries): Maintain thorough case-by-case assessment with multiple sources but no commitment to specific re-evaluation

main_topics.outcome: Motion 22054 nr. 477 on re-evaluating Indonesia export licenses advised against (Ontraden)

main_topics.summary: Debate over restricting exports of dual-use goods (items with both civilian and military applications) to Israel. DENK advocated for restrictions citing genocide risk; the government opposed blanket restrictions on dual-use goods.

party_positions.DENK (Van Baarle): Support restrictions on dual-use goods to Israel
party_positions.Government (De Vries): Oppose blanket restrictions on dual-use goods

main_topics.summary: Debate over the Netherlands' participation in the Aachen Treaty and its implications for weapons export criteria harmonization. SP sought guarantees that acceding to the treaty would not result in stricter export criteria. The government argued that France, Germany, and Spain do not currently have less stringent criteria, making the conditional guarantee contentious.

party_positions.SP (Dobbe): Support accession only with guarantees that no stricter criteria would result
party_positions.Government (De Vries): Dispute that other signatories have less stringent criteria; support treaty participation

main_topics.topic: Dual-use Goods and EU Export Harmonization
main_topics.summary: GroenLinks-PvdA and SP proposed EU-wide restrictions on exports to countries with human rights risks. The government maintained preference for case-by-case assessment rather than categorical restrictions.

party_positions.GroenLinks-PvdA/SP (Teunissen/Dobbe): Support EU-wide restrictions on exports to human rights risk countries

main_topics.topic: Dutch Dependence on Israeli Weapons Industry
main_topics.summary: GroenLinks-PvdA raised concerns about Dutch economic dependence on Israeli weapons suppliers and proposed ending this dependence.

party_positions.GroenLinks-PvdA (Teunissen): Advocate ending Dutch dependence on Israeli weapons industry
party_positions.Government (De Vries): Maintain strategic partnerships based on case-by-case assessment

main_topics.summary: Debate over directing humanitarian spending through local partners versus multilateral institutions. ChristenUnie emphasized local organizations' effectiveness; GroenLinks-PvdA sought clarification that supporting local actors should not reduce support for UN institutions.

party_positions.ChristenUnie (Ceder): Prioritize local organizations for humanitarian aid effectiveness
party_positions.GroenLinks-PvdA (Kröger): Support local actors while maintaining UN institution funding, especially given US multilateral withdrawal

main_topics.outcome: Motion 36180 nr. 191 status not yet determined; humanitarian aid coordination under review

main_topics.summary: D66 called for diplomatic action to ensure humanitarian access to Palestinian territories.

party_positions.D66 (Bamenga): Advocate for diplomatic action ensuring humanitarian access to Palestinian territories

main_topics.outcome: Motion 36180 nr. 190 status not yet determined

main_topics.summary: Debate over the specific sectoral benefits of the Mercosur trade agreement for the Netherlands. PVV challenged D66 to specify which Dutch sectors benefit; D66 cited general consumer and business benefits through reduced duties and bureaucracy.

party_positions.PVV (Markuszower): Question specificity of claimed Mercosur benefits for Dutch sectors
party_positions.D66 (Bamenga): Cite broad consumer and business benefits through trade facilitation

main_topics.outcome: General agreement on trade benefits with disagreement on specificity

main_topics.summary: DENK pressed for concrete measures to ensure monthly export reporting deadlines are met, noting persistent delays. The government refused to commit additional resources, arguing that bureaucratic measures would divert capacity from actual reporting work.

party_positions.DENK (Van Baarle): Demand concrete measures to meet monthly reporting deadlines
party_positions.Government (De Vries): Maintain current two-month publication timeline without diverting resources to administrative measures

main_topics.outcome: Ongoing issue; government maintains current reporting capacity without additional resource allocation

political_dynamics: The session revealed a fundamental divide between the government and opposition parties over arms export policy philosophy. The government (VVD/De Vries) consistently advocated for case-by-case assessment based on individual circumstances, while left-wing and progressive parties (DENK, SP, GroenLinks-PvdA) pushed for categorical restrictions and blanket embargoes based on humanitarian and legal grounds (ICJ findings on genocide, human rights concerns). The government successfully defended its position, with most restrictive motions advised against, though two Sudan-related motions proceeded to parliament. Minor coalitional disagreements emerged between GroenLinks-PvdA and ChristenUnie on humanitarian aid delivery mechanisms, though both supported increased aid. The PVV expressed skepticism about trade agreements, suggesting populist resistance to international commitments. Overall, the government maintained strategic flexibility in export policy against opposition demands for categorical restrictions.
next_steps: Motions 22054 nr. 470 and 22054 nr. 474 on Sudan weapons diversion will be debated and voted on by full parliament
Government to continue case-by-case assessment of weapons exports while defending this approach against calls for embargoes
Export reporting deadlines and capacity to remain under parliamentary scrutiny despite government's resistance to additional resource allocation
Humanitarian access to Palestinian territories and local aid partnership mechanisms to be further developed (pending decisions on motions 36180 nr. 190 and 191)
Indonesia weapons export assessments to proceed under existing review procedures without special re-evaluation based on investigative journalism
Continued monitoring of Dutch economic dependence on Israeli weapons suppliers under regular export licensing reviews
Government to maintain strategic partnerships while responding to parliamentary pressure on human rights concerns in export decisions
